newsitem.title: USA: Sequana says discovers asthma gene.
newsitem.headline: Sequana says discovers asthma gene.

text.p: Sequana Therapeutics Inc said on Wednesday that it had discovered a gene responsible for asthma, providing new clues for improving the diagnosis and treatment of the disease.
Sequana said the discovery was made through its alliance with Boehringer Ingelheim International GmbH.

"Sequana's gene discovery is perhaps this century's most important finding in the etiology of asthma," said Dr. Richard O'Connor, chief of the Division of Asthma, Allergy and Clinical Immunology at Sharp Rees-Stealy Medical Group and Clinical Professor of Pediatrics at University of California, San Diego. "This landmark discovery will bring us one step closer to finding better drugs to address this growing epidemic."
After 2-1/2 years of work, researchers at Sequana were able to isolate the gene, the most common susceptibility gene ever discovered, it said.

"This gene discovery defines for us a fundamental cause of asthma and will help us identify novel points of therapeutic intervention," said Christoph Hohbach, worldwide director of research at Boehringer Ingelheim.
